name: Albuquerque Apparel Center
old_description: Albuquerque Apparel Center is an infrastructure tailored to meet the needs of designers, suppliers, production houses, merchants, and visitors with a wide range of useful customized products and services.  We are New Mexico’s premier venue of clothing and accessory design as well as supplies, services and events.
about:
Albuquerque Apparel Center operates in Albuquerque, New Mexico, as a physical and online hub for the state's apparel and accessory industry. The center was established to connect designers, suppliers, production houses, merchants, and visitors with resources, supplies, employment, and industry-related services.

The center provides a range of services including a networking hub with multi-media promotional advertising and events such as fashion shows and seminars, a retail outlet where designers can sell directly to customers while connecting with wholesale buyers, and an online destination site, NMFashionInfo.com, listing apparel stores, supplies, services, and events across New Mexico. It also runs the AAC School of Fashion Design, offering classes in flat pattern design, draping, sewing, and couture garment construction for all ages, along with mentorship programs for schools and organizations. Custom design and pattern services are available for start-ups and established businesses.

The center serves the broader fashion and apparel industry in New Mexico, targeting independent designers, apparel start-ups, production houses, retail merchants, and educational institutions. It also works with community organizations such as battered women's groups and rehabilitation facilities, providing fashion design classes as a pathway to employment and self-sufficiency.

The center's stated mission is to foster the growth of New Mexico's apparel industry by leveraging the state's unique Southwest, Native American, and Western styles, lower cost of living, and local creative talent. It positions itself as a support system that guides businesses from concept to consumer, aiming to create jobs and retain the economic benefits of New Mexico's distinctive fashion heritage within the state.
